decision.explanation: The provided literature (pmid-20979473) documents a patient with T4N3M1 lung adenocarcinoma harboring an EML4-ALK variant 1 fusion who was treated with crizotinib. At disease progression, molecular analysis identified a somatically acquired ALK C1156Y mutation within the fusion that was absent in the pre-treatment specimen. Functional assays and immunoblotting confirmed that the EML4-ALK C1156Y fusion confers resistance to crizotinib, as the drug failed to reduce tyrosine phosphorylation of the mutant fusion and cytotoxicity assays demonstrated increased resistance compared to wildtype. All component claims regarding the molecular profile, somatic origin, drug exposure, and predictive resistance relationship were confirmed by the verifier.

citations.quote: A 28 year-old patient with T4N3M1 stage lung adenocarcinoma harboring an EML4-ALK variant 1 fusion was treated with crizotinib after failing conventional therapy. The patient achieved a partial response, but progressed after 5 months of treatment. Molecular analysis at relapse identified C1156Y in the ALK kinase domain of the fusion at an allele frequency of 41.8%. This variant was undetected by Sanger sequencing in the tumor collected before crizotinib treatment. Cytotoxicity assays revealed Ba/F3 cells expressing EML4-ALK C1156Y were more resistant to crizontinib than those expressing
EML4-ALK wildtype. Immunoblot demonstrated crizontinib reduced tyrosine phosphorylation of the wildtype fusion, but not the EML4-ALK C1156Y fusion.

output.explanation: The provided literature (pmid-20979473) documents a patient with T4N3M1 lung adenocarcinoma harboring an EML4-ALK variant 1 fusion who was treated with crizotinib. At disease progression, molecular analysis identified a somatically acquired ALK C1156Y mutation within the fusion that was absent in the pre-treatment specimen. Functional assays and immunoblotting confirmed that the EML4-ALK C1156Y fusion confers resistance to crizotinib, as the drug failed to reduce tyrosine phosphorylation of the mutant fusion and cytotoxicity assays demonstrated increased resistance compared to wildtype. All component claims regarding the molecular profile, somatic origin, drug exposure, and predictive resistance relationship were confirmed by the verifier.
